uas_groups.name: Group 1 - Micro/Mini
uas_groups.notes: Highest-density threat class worldwide and the hardest exchange problem: a $500 fiber-optic FPV cannot be economically met with any kinetic interceptor. Reusable EW, smart optics, and acoustic cueing are the only effectors that win the math. Fiber and autonomous variants defeat RF-only defeat systems entirely.

uas_groups.name: Group 2 - Small

swap_c_estimate.size: Two-person lift or small vehicle launch

uas_groups.notes: Fixed-wing ISR and heavier attack payloads. Faster and higher than Group 1, stressing detection timelines for point defense. Threat cost is high enough that T1 attritable interceptors return a strongly favorable exchange.

uas_groups.name: Group 3 - Medium
uas_groups.notes: OWA cruise-missile-like profiles and armed ISR. Note the cost anomaly: Shahed-class OWA sits at the low end of this group's cost band at $30-50K despite Group 3 performance, which is precisely why million-dollar interceptors lose. Handheld EW is ineffective; kinetic or HPM required.

uas_groups.name: Group 4 - Large
uas_groups.notes: Persistent armed ISR. Threat value is high enough that exquisite interceptors are economically justified, inverting the attritable logic. Engagement transitions to traditional air defense; C-sUAS systems contribute cueing only.

uas_groups.name: Group 5 - Largest
uas_groups.notes: Strategic ISR and strike. Defeated by integrated air and missile defense, not C-sUAS systems. Attritable effectors are irrelevant at this tier.
